title: SEC witness: Constitution bans VP Sara Duterte from participating in business
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte is prohibited by the 1987 Constitution to participate in any business during her tenure, a witness from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said Monday.

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte is prohibited by the 1987 Constitution to participate in any business during her tenure, a witness from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said Monday.

SEC Company Registration and Monitoring Department Director Gerardo Fernando Del Rosario made the testimony during Day 27 of the impeachment trial of the Vice President, citing Article 7, Section 13 of the Constitution during the direct examination of private prosecutor Erwin Matib.

“We have a provision sa ating Constitution na nagsasabi na ang Presidente, Vice President, Cabinet members, maging ang kanilang deputies, ay hindi maaring maghold ng ibang opisina, magkaron ng ibang trabaho, mag-engage sa ibang propesyon, magkaroon ng business interest, upang maiwasan po iyong conflict of interest,” Del Rosario replied when Matib asked him if Duterte is allowed to serve as one of the Board of Directors of the companies where she has business interests in based on SEC records.

(We have a Constitutional provision saying that the President, Vice Preisdent, Cabinet members and their deputies, they cannot hold other office, cannot have another job, cannot engage in a different profession, cannot engage in any other profession, cannot have business interest, to avoid conflict of interest.)
These businesses include: Metro City Chow Foods Corporation and City Hall King Chow Foods Corporation, among others.

Article 7, Section 13 of the Constitution states that “The President, Vice-President, the Members of the Cabinet, and their deputies or assistants shall not, unless otherwise provided in this Constitution, hold any other office or employment during their tenure. They shall not, during said tenure, directly or indirectly, practice any other profession, participate in any business, or be financially interested in any contract with, or in any franchise, or special privilege granted by the government or any subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries.”

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero then asked Del Rosario if the phrase “business interests” is explicitly stated in the Constitution, Del Rosario replied that he understood it to mean that the prohibition “to participate in business.”
Defense counsel Justin Gular objected to Matib’s question to Del Rosario by arguing that it calls for conclusion of law and fact.
Escudero, however, allowed Matib to proceed.
“I'll allow it because I'm also interested to find out if they flagged it or not,” the impeachment court presiding officer said.
As of press time, Del Rosario has not mentioned about flagging any business related to the Vice President.—AOL, GMA News
